newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: USTR Barshefsky urges WTO to complete infotech deal.
newsitem.headline: USTR Barshefsky urges WTO to complete infotech deal.

text.p: Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky on Monday urged World Trade Organisation (WTO) ministers to "seize" the opportunity and complete a global agreement on information technology this week.

In a speech at the opening session of the first meeting of WTO ministers, Barshefsky said the Information Technology Agreement (ITA) to eliminate tariffs on a wide variety of computer and telecommunications products would help put less costly technologies in the hands of businesses around the globe, making them more competitive.
"That's why we must reach agreement this week," Barshefsky said. "Remaining issues are ripe for decision. We have an historic opportunity to eliminate tariffs on these products. We must seize it."

She also urged ministers from the 128 WTO member countries to complete global negotiations to open telecommunications markets to more competition. Negotiators are working against a February 15 deadline and Barshefsky urged other countries to follow the example of the United States and Europe and improve their offers.

"With such a short amount of time after this ministerial to conclude this negotiation, we hope all WTO members will contribute meaningfully to an agreement that provides market access and investment opportunities in the 21st century," Barshefsky said.

But she said the United States, which represents 50 percent of the world's global telecommunications revenue, "cannot and we will not, settle for a situation where we are unable to operate in the other half of the world's markets. We are ready to lead by making the first best offer, but we cannot succeed unless others come forward on a mutual basis."
